content.comment_body: Hello, I am experiencing the same issue (see screenshots). My laptop runs Windows 10 with IPv6 Address ::5149:c97a:c8f8:9cfd and IPv4 Address 192.168.0.7. Subnet mask is 255.255.255.0. The [company_name] [product_name] device settings are: IP address 192.168.000.003, subnet mask 255.255.255.000, gateway 192.168.000.000. Please offer advice—screenshots attached. Thank you, [user_name].

Set your PC's network address manually instead of letting [company_name] assign it. If your IPs match as described, this should work. Can you successfully ping the [product_name]? (Open command prompt and run: ping 192.168.0.3)
Here are the results from pinging the PLC as suggested: Pinging 192.168.0.3; Reply times vary (6ms to 2361ms), all packets received, no loss. What solution is recommended?
Both devices are connected to the same network since ping is successful. Have you selected the correct hardware in your configuration? (Try Ctrl+H)
I'm using a single PLC, connected directly to my laptop via the ethernet cable included in the [company_name] starter kit. Please refer to the attached images.

Check if your device is a standard 0BA8 (FS03) or FS04 model—it's indicated on the front plate. If FS04, make sure to select this option in the drop-down menu. FS04 requires [product_name] [version_no].

The packaging label notes: FS: 04, FW: V1.81.01, plus compliance markings. Specifications: logic module, 8 digital inputs (4 analog), 4 digital outputs, [product_name] model 12/24RCE. Mentioned '[product_name] [version_no]'—what is this? For context, I've wired the unit to four bulbs and four switches and written a program to control them. The earth wire isn’t connected but power is supplied when connecting the industrial ethernet cable. Thanks for your assistance.

You’re using the FS04 model. [product_name] refers to the programming software for the PLC. You need [version_no]—check via Help > About. If using an older version, it’s free to update. The latest version can be downloaded at [url]. Remember: Select FS04 in your hardware settings before uploading, otherwise it won't function. See attached guidance.

I updated the programming software to [version_no] and can now transfer my program from PC to [product_name]. Thanks a lot. This is my first time programming and wiring a PLC, so I’m learning. After putting the [product_name] in RUN mode, it shows ''Sat 00:00 2000-01-01.'' Is this the default date? What should I do next to execute my program?

During the online test, an error appeared: ''Online test failed. The hardware type in [product_name] programming software does not match the connected device.'' However, simulation mode worked. See attached screenshot. Please assist.

After using Ctrl+H and selecting FS04 as hardware, the online test succeeded. Attached is my circuit diagram: the design powers one light at a time with a single stop button for all four. A normally closed stop button is used to interrupt power, but I need to keep it pressed while pressing the start buttons. Why do I need to hold the normally closed push button to enable ladder rungs? I've been told that even if a normally closed momentary push button is shown in the ladder diagram, wiring to the PLC should be normally open. Is that true—and why? Thanks for your continuous help. Kind regards, [user_name].

I've set the correct date/time on the device and replaced normally closed stop buttons with normally open push buttons in the ladder diagram. In simulation, they’re defined as normally closed (break contact). Now, both simulation and online tests work as expected. Ladder diagram attached. Thanks and regards, [user_name].

I haven't heard that before—it’s interesting. Glad most issues are now resolved. I’m not well-versed in ladder programming, so I won’t comment further. If you wish, upload the .lsc file (please zip it first).
Hello, I have the same issue: subnet matches on PC and device but still cannot transfer. I'm using [product_name] programming software [version_no], but no improvement. Any advice is welcome.
What are the IP address and subnet mask of your PC? What are the IP address and subnet mask of the [product_name]?
Hi. My computer’s IPv4 address is 192.168.1.65 with subnet 255.255.255.0. Device IP is 192.168.000.002 with subnet 255.255.255.000.
Change the [product_name] IP address from 192.168.000.002 to 192.168.001.002. The subnet mask is fine.
That solved the issue—thank you!
Glad to hear it—you're welcome.

Hi. I'm experiencing the same issue: every time I try to connect [product_name] with my PC, I get the message that IP addresses are not in the same subnet. My PC IP is 192.168.0.163, subnet mask 255.255.255.0. Device IP is 192.168.000.003, subnet mask 255.255.255.000. Please suggest next steps.
Both devices share the same network: 192.168.000.xxx

analysis.insight_summary: The main challenge was getting a PC to communicate with a [product_name] PLC, impeded by mismatches between device versions and programming software, as well as network configuration. Updating the software and matching hardware resolved the primary issue, but users encountered additional concerns such as running the program and setting device time/date. Error messages within the software lacked clarity, causing confusion.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward connectivity and program transfer between their PC and PLC, with minimal configuration or compatibility issues. They want clear, actionable feedback from the software regarding hardware compatibility and guidance for first-time setup steps including time and date settings.
